title: Glen Industries Ltd - 544444 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Glen Industries H1 FY27 revenue rose 20.66% to INR115.30 crores and net profit 31.36% to INR10.91 crores, with new Howrah capacity now slipping to April 2027.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 20.66% YoY to INR115.30 crores, EBITDA rose 12.47% to INR22.71 crores at a 19.5% margin, and PAT grew 31.36% to INR10.91 crores. Management said the new Howrah facility, originally expected to start earlier, will now begin injection moulding around January 2027 with all three divisions in production by April 2027. Management cut its FY27 revenue outlook to about INR225-230 crores, citing the delay, and said raw material costs have eased slightly from peak levels.

financial_highlights.change: +31.36% YoY vs INR8.31 crores; net margin 9.37%

financial_highlights.value: Thin wall food containers 80.75%, PLA straws 12.63%, paper straws 6.62%
Revenue INR203.13 crores (+19.02%); net profit INR16.5 crores

segments.name: Thin wall food containers
segments.commentary: Contributed 80.75% of H1 FY27 revenue; about 50% of this product is exported, per management.

segments.name: PLA straws
segments.commentary: Contributed 12.63% of H1 FY27 revenue; monthly capacity 160 MT.

segments.name: Paper straws
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.62% of H1 FY27 revenue; monthly capacity 95 MT. Paper cups and paper food containers to be added at the new Howrah plant.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue now guided at about INR225-230 crores (earlier INR350 crores target, of which about INR125 crores was from the new facility); management expects at most INR25-40 crores from the new facility this year.
H2 FY27 revenue guided at about INR115 crores, taking FY27 to about INR230 crores; revenue could reach INR245-250 crores with marginal new-project injection output.

New facility to start injection moulding around January 2027 (management said it is pushing for this), with thermoforming and paper products following; all three divisions in production by April 2027.

Stabilisation expected 5-6 months after start, with full run-rate around September-October 2027; FY28 turnover guided at INR400-500 crores; full impact of the expansion expected in FY29 at about INR550 crores.

EBITDA margin guided at 18-19% at steady state; FY29 PAT estimated at about INR50-55 crores at INR550 crores revenue. Management said EBITDA of INR95-100 crores holds regardless of raw material price movements.
Target of INR1,000 crores turnover by 2030, with next project planning to start after a 3-4 month cooling period following the new facility's start.
capex_capacity: Total capex about INR130 crores (INR100.49 crores for new facilities and production lines, per management); capex unchanged.
Post-expansion capacity: 21,095 MT/year of food containers (incl. additional 13,109 MT/year via injection and thermoforming) and 7,696 MT/year of new paper products capacity.
Existing monthly capacity: 665 MT thin wall food containers, 160 MT PLA straws, 95 MT paper straws at the 90,000 sq ft Dhulagarh, Howrah facility.

Delay attributed to election SIR process, government machinery slowdown, severe West Bengal monsoon (30% excess rain vs -12% nationally), and civil work challenges from February 2026 to October 2026; machines are in warehouse or ready in China awaiting shipment.
Depreciation: existing about INR7 crores/year, rising to INR17-18 crores after the project (INR10-11 crores incremental).
demand_pricing: Raw material costs rose from about INR100/kg before the Gulf/Middle East conflict to about INR160 now; selling prices moved from about INR200 to INR260-270 (about 35%), applied in stages from April to August.
Management said customers have no option to push back as no supplier can absorb such costs; margin percentages compressed by about 1-2 points, while absolute per-MT value addition held.
Management said raw material prices have begun easing from October and that revenue may see a marginal reduction, with no material impact on absolute profitability.

Exports of about 26% of revenue; target to raise export share to about 35%. Major growth focus on Europe and North America (Canada and Mexico inquiries from PEC Expo USA), with Southeast Asia and Middle East not seen as viable.

Management said the company prices above market and that demand is not a constraint for new capacity; the company is adding thermoforming (fruit, bakery, namkeen, meal trays) and IML (sweets, ice cream, candy) lines. Customer base to remain the same across injection, thermoforming and paper.

qa_highlights.question: Why were margins sustained despite the crude-linked raw material spike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage margins compressed by about 1-2 points because value addition per tonne is fixed in absolute terms; management tracks gross profit and EBITDA per MT and was asked to disclose on that basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the new facility slip about 6 months and when will it reach full capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay blamed on election SIR process, a government slowdown and a severe monsoon in West Bengal; full run-rate expected around September-October 2027, with full capacity impact in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue outlook versus the earlier INR350 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new facility will contribute at most INR25 crores in FY27, so FY27 revenue is now expected at about INR225-230 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY29 PAT outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: On INR550 crores revenue at 18% EBITDA margin, less about INR15 crores interest, INR18 crores depreciation and about INR14 crores tax, PAT of about INR50-55 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How is debt and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing term loan negligible; about INR5 crores plus a new INR50 crores bank term loan (INR55 crores total, repayable over 7 years) at 8-8.5%. Working capital bank debt about INR80 crores. Management has no current plan to raise additional equity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company return to margin improvement or raise prices further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin expansion is not expected; growth will be horizontal, with EBITDA margin at 18-19% and 18% as the conservative case.

risks_watch: Commissioning timing: the injection line must start by January 2027 and all divisions by April 2027; the project has already slipped about 6 months and machines are still in China.
FY27 guidance cut to about INR225-230 crores from the earlier INR350 crore target, with H2 revenue flat-to-lower as raw material prices ease.
Pricing reversal: management said prices will move down with raw material costs, which could lower revenue while EBITDA is claimed to be stable at INR95-100 crores.
Export share (26%) and geopolitical and freight exposure; management said exports are not affected but volumes depend on the new capacity.
Return on capital not calculated; management said it expects it will not be below 15%. Future INR1,000 crore turnover target by 2030 is not yet supported by a project plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and margins, but defensive on the project timeline, which management attributed to external causes; several answers were approximate (ROCE not calculated, capex unchanged) and some numbers were corrected or restated during the call.
key_quotes: So we hope to complete process setting and start production by this April 2027 in all the three divisions.
We already price our products higher than the market.
Margin improvement will not take place. Only horizontal growth of revenue will take place, but margin improvement is not expected because we already have optimized the margin, whatever can be done.
On the most optimistic side, I put always 18%.

adds.what: New Howrah facility: injection moulding, thermoforming, IML lines and paper products (cups, food containers); 13,109 MT/yr additional food container capacity an

growth.why: FY27 revenue cut to about INR225-230 crore (from INR350 crore target), implying roughly 13% growth on FY26's INR203 crore; delivery rests on the Howrah plant slipping to injection start around January 2027 and all divisions by April 2027, with only INR25-40 crore expected from it this year and H1 growth of 20.66% driven partly by 35% price hikes.

quality.why: Revenue rose 20.66% to INR115.30 crores, and the brief attributes the rise mainly to a roughly 35% selling-price increase passed through from raw material costs (INR200 to INR260-270/kg), not to volume, which is not quantified. Management expects price to reverse as raw material eases, so revenue growth will fade in H2 and FY27 guidance was cut to INR225-230 crores.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said margin expansion is not expected: EBITDA margin is guided at 18-19% at steady state, versus 19.5% in H1 FY27 and percentage margins already compressed 1-2 points by raw material inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Injection start ~Jan 2027; all divisions by Apr 2027
rows.why: Howrah plant (INR100.49 crore new lines, machines in warehouse or ready in China) is under construction; slipped ~6 months, with injection targeted for January 2027 and full run-rate around Sep-Oct 2027, post-expansion capacity 21,095 MT/yr food containers and 7,696 MT/yr paper.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volumes depend on the new lines: 13,109 MT/yr added food container capacity and 7,696 MT/yr paper capacity, with FY28 turnover guided at INR400-500 crore versus about INR230 crore in FY27 and demand described as not a constraint.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Total capex held at about INR130 crore and management said the next project only starts after a 3-4 month cooling period following the new facility's start, so no fresh capex is signalled within 2-4 quarters; utilisation is 665 MT/month for thin wall containers, which is high but no new plant is planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue could reach INR245-250 crore in FY27 with marginal injection output, and FY28 turnover is guided at INR400-500 crore, so upside depends on faster start-up of the new lines.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue already cut to INR225-230 crore from INR350 crore; new facility contributes only INR25-40 crore this year and H2 FY27 guided at about INR115 crore, with raw material prices easing and revenue set to fall as prices pass through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Injection moulding (Jan 2027), thermoforming (fruit, bakery, namkeen, meal trays), IML (sweets, ice cream, candy) and paper cups/food containers to follow at the new Howrah plant, with all divisions by April 2027.

rows.label: Export share rise to ~35% (Europe, North America)
rows.why: Exports were 26.34% of H1 FY27 revenue with a target of about 35%; Canada and Mexico inquiries from PEC Expo USA are not yet firm orders.

rows.label: New INR50 crore term loan at 8-8.5% for project
rows.why: Total project debt of INR55 crore (repayable over 7 years) plus about INR80 crore working capital debt will add interest cost, with FY29 interest estimated at about INR15 crore; no equity raise is planned.

rows.label: Raw material-linked price pass-back
rows.why: Selling prices rose about 35% (INR200 to INR260-270/kg) while raw material moved from INR100 to INR160/kg; management said prices will ease with raw material costs and revenue may see a marginal reduction.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing and the 18-19% margin band but defensive on the project delay, which it attributed to elections, monsoon and civil works; analysts pressed on the revenue cut from INR350 crore to INR225-230 crore and on the approximate numbers given.
